Investigated concepts and ideas relating to CPS architectures that enable design support showed the need to properly address inherent CPS complexity. We also found a need to focus validation activities on achieved outcomes for targeted design support user groups as well as people affected by the CPS.
records.authors: Jost, Thomas Ernst; Heininger, Richard; Stary, Christian

records.title: An overview: Current trends of Real-time monitoring and pressure vessel failure prediction using artificial intelligence (AI) and internet of things (IOT)
records.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the monitoring and maintenance of pressure vessels indicates a substantial progress across multiple industries. This article offers a summary of current developments in the application of advanced technology for fault detection, failure prediction, and maintenance optimization. This analysis of research trends from 2015 to 2025 highlights the shortcomings in predicting pressure vessel failures with AI and IoT technology. Despite significant advancements, obstacles persist, including the lack of high-quality datasets, cybersecurity issues and high implementation costs, and the complexities of system integration remain critical issues that must be addressed. In conclusion, By synthesizing these advancements, this work underscores AI's potential to accelerate development, reduce costs, and improve pressure vessels performance, while advocating for physics-informed models, robust datasets, and regulatory alignment to facilitate industrial adoption.
records.authors: Imron, Jefri; Setiyana, Budi; Sulardjaka, Sulardjaka

records.title: Copper industrial product monitoring system based on digital twin technology
records.abstract: This paper describes the design of a monitoring system for copper industrial products that uses digital twin technology. The system's objective is to monitor the dimensions and surface conditions of copper components in industrial settings accurately. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the system's structure and functionality, including the design of the visualization dashboard. It also explains the implementation of the data acquisition, processing, analysis, and visualization modules. Additionally, this text discusses the use of visual detection techniques for dimension inspection and defect recognition in detail. The system's architecture incorporates advanced sensing technologies and computational algorithms to ensure accurate monitoring and assessment of copper product attributes.
records.authors: Li, Can; Zhu, Zhengyuan; Mao, Xiang

records.title: Key technology of digital twin modeling for production process of flexible production line based on data
records.abstract: This paper introduces a digital twin framework designed for flexible production lines. The framework aims to achieve real-time data collection and transmission in physical space through the development of a virtual simulation system, enabling synchronized motion with physical entities. It provides functions such as visual management, real-time monitoring, and data statistical analysis for flexible production lines. Additionally, it supports offline simulation to verify, evaluate, and optimize production plans. The overall architecture includes the data layer, model layer, technology development layer, system function layer, and application presentation layer. The process constraint [1] rule model is designed to model both hard and soft constraints in the production process, including various rules at the equipment and unit levels, ensuring the standardization and flexibility of the production process.
records.authors: Du, Yinfu; Zhou, Lili; Zhang, Jianping

records.title: It's a Big Tiny(ML) World in Industry 4.0 and 5.0
records.abstract: As machine learning becomes more prevalent, edge computing has become more important towards the goal of ubiquitous AI. In order to understand the landscape, we propose a new taxonomy for studying current technologies that can be optimized for resource-constrained devices, specifically deploying TinyML. Through an organized investigation, we aim to introduce new insights into the panorama of current research TinyML implementations and applications in Industry 4.0 and 5.0. This work identifies the most common techniques and tools, along with challenges and opportunities for future developments and proposes a taxonomy where the main axis is in field model adaptability, which serves the shift to ubiquitous computing in Industry 4.0/5.0.
records.authors: Torres Medina, Karen T.; S\'{a}nchez Orozco, Daniela E.; Mera Collantes, Mar\'{\i}a I.

records.title: Design and Optimization of Intelligent Manufacturing System in Cigarette Factory
records.abstract: With the advent of the Industry 4.0 era, intelligent manufacturing has become a key force in promoting the transformation and upgrading of the manufacturing industry. As an important part of the traditional manufacturing industry, cigarette factories must improve production efficiency, optimize product quality, and reduce operating costs. This paper carries out a design and optimization study for the cigarette factory intelligent manufacturing system, analyzes the shortcomings of the existing system, puts forward the principles and methods for the design of the overall architecture of the cigarette factory intelligent manufacturing system, including the facility layer, the edge layer, the basic service layer, the platform service layer, and the display interaction, and describes in detail the technological implementation and functional modules of each layer. In addition, this paper proposes system optimization strategies and methods for meeting the actual needs of cigarette factories. Through the implementation of these strategies, it aims to achieve the optimization goals of improving production efficiency, enhancing product quality, reducing production costs, and enhancing market competitiveness. Finally, through practical application, it is verified that the optimized intelligent manufacturing system can effectively improve production efficiency and quality level.
records.authors: Tang, Xuechao; Zhou, Leting; Yuan, Hongyu; Wang, Peichen; Huang, Wenchao; Zhao, Wenkun; Sun, Xiaorui

records.title: SERA – An AI Driven Re-Programmable Simulation Environment for Explainable Resiliency Analysis in Cyber-Physical Systems
records.abstract: Testbeds are a practical way to perform security exercises on cyberphysical systems (CPS) to understand vulnerabilities and the progression/ impact of cyber-attacks on CPS safety. Most CPS testbeds use a hardware-in-the-loop architecture. However, it limits the testbed's ability to easily reconfigure with new features, new capabilities and new vulnerabilities. Moreover, cyber attacks recreated within the testbed can potentially damage the hardware that the cyber attack targets. These factors suggest a software-based testbed for CPS cyber security and resiliency research. In this paper, we present SERA, an AI-driven, software-based simulation environment for resiliency analysis in CPS. It is specifically geared towards explainable resiliency analysis using the Resiliency Graph model proposed by Bashir et al. [3] and is fully reconfigurable and extendable for experimentation on different types of CPSes.
records.authors: Podder, Rakesh; Ray, Indrajit

records.title: Prospects for Predictive Maintenance and Intelligent Workover Operations in Oil and Gas Well Sites
records.abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerated global energy structure transformation and digitalization in the oil and gas industry, traditional maintenance models can hardly meet the requirements of efficient, safe, and economical modern wellsite operations. This paper systematically explores the theoretical framework, technical system, and integration path of predictive maintenance and intelligent workover operations in oil and gas wellsites. The study shows that predictive maintenance, centered on real-time sensing, artificial intelligence, digital twin, and automation technologies, has established a closed-loop feedback mechanism from condition perception to fault early warning, driving a paradigm shift in maintenance strategies from "time-series driven" to "condition driven"; intelligent workover operations, relying on smart equipment, data-driven decision-making, and remote collaboration, have restructured operational processes and execution logic. The in-depth integration of the two has formed an integrated operation and maintenance system of "perception-prediction-decision-execution". However, current challenges include data heterogeneity, model interpretability, system integration security, and lack of interdisciplinary talents. Based on this, the paper proposes development paths such as strengthening data governance, advancing technical standardization, enhancing human-machine collaboration, and implementing in phases. The research concludes that predictive maintenance and intelligent workover operations are core drivers for the oil and gas industry to transform and upgrade towards "unmanned, intelligent, and green" development, and hold significant strategic importance for safeguarding future energy security.
records.authors: Zhang, Xuesong; Li, Jianming; Cao, Peng; Chen, Defei; Li, Qiang

records.title: Digital Twin: State-of-the-Art and Future Perspectives
records.abstract: In the midst of the swift advance of informatization, digital twin technology has garnered escalating attention. Synthesizing the current research landscape and cutting-edge developments in digital twin technology is crucial for propelling its scholarly exploration. This study employs a methodological fusion of scientometrics and knowledge graph analysis to comprehensively encapsulate the research accomplishments of digital twin technology across extant scientific domains. It visually dissects 4,954 articles pertaining to digital twins within the Web of Science core dataset, spanning the decade from 2014 to 2024. Leveraging keyword cluster analysis, the research identifies the focal areas that have captivated researchers in recent years, along with the prevailing research trends. Building upon this foundation, the paper delineates the pivotal technologies underpinning digital twins. Ultimately, the study offers strategic recommendations for the evolutionary trajectory of digital twin technology, aspiring to furnish a scientific touchstone for global digital twin research endeavors.
records.authors: Xu, Qianwen; Wang, Jingchao; Gao, Wei; Ren, Shuangyin; Li, Zhongbo

records.title: Data Centers Manufacturing Steel: Rethinking Industrial Networks in the Age of IT
records.abstract: Industrial networks are undergoing a radical shift from closed, static OT environments towards open networks that integrate IT and OT. This shift applies IT operation principles to OT environments, such as virtualizing Programmable Logic Controllers and using Artificial Intelligence to increase production and process efficiency. While there is a huge effort to integrate IT principles, this paper demonstrates that IT/OT convergence remains an underexplored area of research, leaving out critical research opportunities for future networking systems. We identify three core challenges: timing constraints, service availability, and changing network traffic characteristics. For each challenge, we provide a concrete use case that demonstrates early findings and opens up new avenues for research within SIGCOMM.
records.authors: Mitsakis, Nikolaos; Reisacher, Marco; Eichholz, Matthias; Breiting, Yannic; Albrecht, Harald; Blenk, Andreas; Hohlfeld, Oliver

records.title: Practical design and implementation of an augmented reality based digital twin
records.abstract: This paper presents a practical example of design and implementation of an augmented reality based digital twin of moving wheeled robots in an indoor environment. The architecture developed is based on the RAMI (Reference Architectural Model Industry 4.0) framework and integrates both the physical and the digital twins, allowing continuous data exchange and real-time feedback loops between the two twins. From the physical twin perspective, the use of augmented reality (AR) headsets and position sensors enables to track the movement of the wheeled robots. The interest of the chosen architecture is a seamless communication of the decision and user interfacing elements including the AR headsets and the fulfilment layers of the digital twin. The current developed modules are deployed at a laboratory scale. The perspective of this work is an upscale to larger rooms and more industrial robots.
records.authors: Protin, Lionel; Aggoune-Mtalaa, Wassila; Kavka, Carlos

records.title: Predicted In-Sync Digital Twin for Fast Decision Making
records.abstract: In Industry 4.0, Digital Twins enable real-time monitoring and decision-making through a digital replica of physical systems. However, their effectiveness depends on the ability to timely mirror the corresponding system's behavior. While systems are subject to unbounded delays, decisions must often be taken within a strict time window. In critical contexts, waiting for accurate data is crucial, as decisions based on stale data could be dangerous. Conversely, in safer contexts, such as Industry 4.0, where machines are equipped with autonomous safety mechanisms, decisions could be made in a timely manner with a proper mechanism to adjust the Digital Twin state and enhance production line resilience. In this work, we propose a data-driven method to enhance Digital Twin synchronization, in presence of delay bound, by ensuring the timely availability of data when required to support more informed decisions. We validate the approach through an industrial use case featuring a packaging line and a KUKA LBR iiwa collaborative robot. This approach moves towards an ''Always In-Sync'' Digital Twin capable of proactive, trustworthy decision-making in dynamic industrial environments.
records.authors: Colarusso, Carmine; Falco, Ida; Goglia, Lorenzo; Perugini, Pio Antonio; Zimeo, Eugenio

records.title: Visualization Analysis of Research Trends in Machine Learning for Pump Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis Based on CiteSpace
records.abstract: Pump systems are key energy-consuming equipment in industrial production, municipal infrastructure and agriculture, and improving their operating efficiency is essential for achieving low-carbon and intelligent manufacturing goals. In recent years, machine learning has been increasingly adopted to support condition monitoring, fault diagnosis and operation optimization of pumps, yet the overall research landscape of this emerging field has not been systematically reviewed. This study employs bibliometric methods integrated with information visualization techniques to analyze the research status and developmental trends of machine learning for pump systems. Using the Web of Science Core Collection as the data source, publications from 2007 to 2025 are retrieved and examined with CiteSpace to construct and interpret scientific knowledge graphs, including publication trends, co-authorship networks, institutional and national collaboration patterns, keyword co-occurrence clusters and keyword bursts. The results reveal a rapid expansion of research activity since 2016, a layered knowledge structure linking centrifugal pump design, fault diagnosis, predictive maintenance and energy-efficient operation, and a clear evolution from traditional machine learning and support vector machines to deep learning, convolutional neural networks and intelligent optimization algorithms. These findings clarify the technical pathways through which machine learning supports the intelligent, low-carbon transformation of pump systems, highlight current limitations in data coverage, model interpretability and cross-scenario adaptability, and provide a quantitative evidence base for future research directions and policy making.
records.authors: Wang, Rui; Liang, Xiuying; Liu, Ren

records.title: Energy-Efficient Resource Management in Microservices-Based Fog and Edge Computing: State-of-the-Art and Future Directions
records.abstract: The exponential growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has intensified the demand for efficient and responsive services. To address this demand, fog and edge computing have emerged as distributed paradigms that bring computational resources closer to end users, reducing latency, bandwidth limitations, and energy consumption. However, these paradigms present challenges in resource management due to resource constraints, computational heterogeneity, dynamic workloads, and diverse Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. This article presents a comprehensive survey of state-of-the-art resource management strategies in microservices-based fog and edge computing, focusing on energy-efficient solutions. We systematically review and classify over 136 studies (2020–2024) into five key subdomains: service placement, resource provisioning, task scheduling and offloading, resource allocation, and instance selection. Our categorization is based on optimization techniques, targeted objectives, and the strengths and limitations of each approach. Additionally, we examine existing surveys, identifying unresolved challenges and gaps in the literature. By highlighting the lack of synergy among fundamental resource management components, we outline promising research directions leveraging AI-driven optimization, quantum computing, and serverless computing. This survey serves as a comprehensive reference for researchers and practitioners, providing a unified, energy-aware perspective on resource management in microservices-based fog and edge computing, and paving the way for more integrated, efficient, and sustainable future solutions.
records.authors: Vali, Ali Akbar; Azizi, Sadoon; Shojafar, Mohammad; Buyya, Rajkumar

records.title: Aegis-5: A Hybrid Ensemble Framework for Intrusion Detection in Industry 5.0 Driven Smart Manufacturing Environment
records.abstract: Industry 5.0 represents a transformative paradigm that emphasizes synergy between human expertise, intelligent systems, and hyper connected cyber-physical environments. While this evolution fosters personalized automation and resilient production, it also amplifies the cybersecurity risks inherent in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) infrastructures. In this research, we present Aegis-5 a novel adaptive hybrid ensemble framework explicitly designed for intrusion detection in Industry 5.0-enabled smart manufacturing ecosystems. The proposed model integrates five diverse classifiers Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, SVM, and K-Nearest Neighbors using a dynamic weighting strategy guided by per-class precision, recall, and F1-score performance in real time. A meta-learner further synthesizes these predictions to enhance robustness against sophisticated and zero-day attacks. To ensure relevance and reliability, we evaluate the model using two benchmark IIoT datasets: IoT-23 and CIC-IoT 2023, both of which capture a broad spectrum of real-world industrial threats. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves superior performance, with accuracy rates of 99.98% on IoT-23 and 99.95% on CIC-IoT 2023, coupled with precision (99.97%, 99.93%), recall (99.96%, 99.92%), and F1-score (99.96%, 99.93%) respectively., significantly reduces false positives, and adapts effectively to evolving attack behaviors. By aligning intelligent anomaly detection with the responsiveness and adaptability required by Industry 5.0, Aegis-5 offers a scalable, real-time, and practical cybersecurity solution for next-generation industrial systems.
records.authors: Govindarajan, Vijay; Ahmed, Faraz; Faheem, Zaid Bin; Bilal, Muhammad; Ayadi, Manel; Ali, Jehad

records.title: Optimal graph partitioning for time-sensitive flow scheduling towards digital twin networks
records.abstract: The growing maturity of Digital Twin (DT) technology represents a quantum leap towards the realisation of Industry 4.0 and beyond. DT refers to virtual representations (in a virtual space) of physical objects/processes/systems (in a physical space), where information is regularly exchanged between them to enable real-time remote control and monitoring. DT will significantly improve product life-cycles and will transform industries such as smart manufacturing, smart transportation, and so forth. Digital Twin Networks (DTNs) are envisaged to be the norm where multiple DTs are logically connected to their respective physical objects, forming a many-to-many communication relationship. Strict real-time communication for bi-directional data flows is required in DTNs for DTs to accurately reflect the changes in the physical objects, and vice-versa. One potential candidate to achieve real-time data transmission is Time Sensitive Networking (TSN). The IEEE 802.1Q working group has developed a set of TSN standards to facilitate data transmissions that require low-latency, high availability and reliability. In TSN, the Central Network Controller (CNC) computes the schedule of frame transmission. However, the computational time required can exponentially increase as the number of nodes and data flows increases (already typical in industrial environments and will increase exponentially with DTNs). In this paper, we propose a novel technique using multi-level graph partitioning theory with Integer Linear Programming (ILP) to facilitate TSN scheduling. Our results demonstrated significant improvements in computational time and the success rate of scheduled data flows in complex networks where there are up to 100 nodes and 350 data flows.
records.authors: Wang, Shuo; Kua, Jonathan; Jin, Jiong; Kulkarni, Ambarish; Jayaraman, Prem Prakash; Cao, Xianghui

records.title: A Digital Twin Environment for 5G Vehicle-to-Everything: Architecture and Open Issues
records.abstract: The advent of 5G Vehicle-to-Everything (5G-V2X) technology has revolutionized daily life and the economy. However, the complexity of testing 5G-V2X systems in lab and field settings along with the development cost is increasingly challenging. To overcome these issues, the paper proposes the use of Digital Twin technology, which offers a precise, accurate, and controllable lab-based representation of real-world test conditions. The main idea is to design an open-ended digital twin architecture specifically tailored for 5G-V2X, with the aim of fostering innovation in various aspects of autonomous driving. Considering the recent improvement in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) and Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) technologies in the proposed architecture, it not only facilitates the development and testing of diverse and sophisticated network and communication layers solutions and applications, but also provides a real-time environment to evaluate new artificial intelligence (AI) methods, data and model sharing, and progress measurement in the field of 5G-V2X.
records.authors: Adarbah, Haitham Y.; Sookhak, Mehdi; Atiquzzaman, Mohammed

records.title: Special Session: Digital Technologies for Sustainability: Research Challenges and Opportunities
records.abstract: This paper presents an integrative exploration of key digital technologies instrumental in enabling the global green transition. In view of ambitious climate neutrality targets, it underscores the complex interplay between these technologies, policy implications, research challenges, and real-world applications in building a sustainable, low-carbon solutions. From a policy perspective, the paper delves into the systemic opportunities and challenges, providing valuable insights for various stakeholders. The discussion also encompasses pivotal research areas necessitated by the convergence of digital technologies and sustainable practices, emphasizing the need for a multi-disciplinary approach. Further, the paper identifies the practical applications of digital technologies across a range of sectors, highlighting several illustrative case studies, drawing lessons for future implementations. It concludes with forward-looking recommendations, stressing the significance of coherent policy coordination, public engagement, and global cooperation in furthering the digital-led green transition.
records.authors: Pop, Paul; Graulund, Christian; Yeh, Sonia; Torngren, Martin

records.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Collaborative Data-access Enablers in the IIoT
records.abstract: The scope of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has stretched beyond manufacturing to include energy, healthcare, transportation, and all that tomorrow’s smart cities will entail. The realm of IIoT includes smart sensors, actuators, programmable logic controllers, distributed control systems (DCS), embedded devices, supervisory control, and data acquisition systems—all produced by manufacturers for different purposes and with different data structures and formats; designed according to different standards and made to follow different protocols. In this sea of incompatibility, how can we flexibly acquire these heterogeneous data, and how can we uniformly structure them to suit thousands of different applications? In this article, we survey the four pillars of information science that enable collaborative data access in an IIoT—standardization, data acquisition, data fusion, and scalable architecture—to provide an up-to-date audit of current research in the field. Here, standardization in IIoT relies on standards and technologies to make things communicative; data acquisition attempts to transparently collect data through plug-and-play architectures, reconfigurable schemes, or hardware expansion; data fusion refers to the techniques and strategies for overcoming heterogeneity in data formats and sources; and scalable architecture provides basic techniques to support heterogeneous requirements. The article also concludes with an overview of the frontier researches and emerging technologies for supporting or challenging data access from the aspects of 5G, machine learning, blockchain, and semantic web.
records.authors: Sun, Danfeng; Hu, Junjie; Wu, Huifeng; Wu, Jia; Yang, Jian; Sheng, Quan Z.; Dustdar, Schahram

records.title: A Survey of Cloud-Edge Collaborative Scheduling Strategies for Cyber-Physical Production Systems
records.abstract: Accompanied by the rapid integration of information technology, communication technology and control technology, the industrial control system is gradually evolving into a cyber-physical production system(CPPS), with flexibilization and intelligence as its main goals. CPPS is a system that integrates computer science, information technology and physical manufacturing processes, organically combines digital manufacturing and physical manufacturing, and realizes real-time monitoring, intelligent manufacturing and flexible production. Cloud-edge collaborative CPPS, as the main method and foundation of CPPSs, can ensure the real-time and reliable operation of dynamic tasks through intelligent decision-making on the edge, which provides a new solution for flexibilization and intelligence and is a common research hotspot between industries and academics. In this paper, we provide a survey of cloud-edge collaborative scheduling strategies for CPPSs. First, we introduce CPPS, a cyber-physical production system empowered by cloud-edge collaborative technology. Then, the current research situations and problems faced by domestic and international studies on CPPS cloud-edge collaborative scheduling technology are reviewed, and on this basis, the scheduling requirements, optimization objectives and other multiple perspectives are analyzed and compared. Finally, future research directions are summarized and the outlook for existing methods and problems of CPPS cloud-edge collaborative scheduling techniques is given.
records.authors: Yu, Xiaoqian; Xia, Changqing; Zeng, Jing; Xu, Chi; Jin, Xi

records.title: An Entanglement-Aware Middleware for Digital Twins
records.abstract: The development of the Digital Twin (DT) approach is tilting research from initial approaches that aim at promoting early adoption to sophisticated attempts to develop, deploy, and maintain applications based on DTs. In this context, we propose a highly dynamic and distributed ecosystem where containerized DTs co-evolve with an orchestration middleware. DTs provide digitalized representations of the targeted physical systems, while the orchestration middleware monitors and re-configures the deployed DTs in light of application constraints, available resources, and the quality of cyber-physical entanglement. First, we lay out the reference scenario. Then, we discuss the limitations of current approaches and identify a set of requirements that shape both DTs and the orchestration middleware. Subsequently, we describe a blueprint architecture that meets those requirements. Finally, we report empirical evidence on both the feasibility and the effectiveness of a proof-of-concept implementation of the proposed ecosystem.
records.authors: Bellavista, Paolo; Bicocchi, Nicola; Fogli, Mattia; Giannelli, Carlo; Mamei, Marco; Picone, Marco

records.title: Cloud2Things 2025: From Cloud to Things - towards the convergence of IoT, Edge and Cloud Computing
records.abstract: The growing complexity and demand for ubiquitous applications, driven by the widespread adoption of smartphones, wearables, and IoT devices, requires dynamic and scalable computing support. The Computing Continuum, spanning IoT, Edge, and Cloud resources, offers a unified infrastructure to meet these needs by enabling seamless, context-aware, and low-latency service delivery. The Cloud2Things Workshop explores how the continuum can support the development and deployment of ubiquitous applications. It invites contributions that address resource orchestration, adaptive service provisioning, distributed AI, big data processing, and security across heterogeneous environments. Through technical presentations and discussion, the workshop aims to advance the integration of the continuum into a cohesive, pervasive computing fabric capable of supporting next-generation ubiquitous services.
records.authors: Di Modica, Giuseppe; Galletta, Antonino; Bellavista, Paolo; Konstantinou, Ioannis; Catalfamo, Alessio

records.title: Machine Learning-Driven Predictive Maintenance for China's Large Aircraft: Theories, Challenges, and Strategic Applications
records.abstract: With the rapid development of China's aviation industry, domestically produced large aircraft are gradually emerging in the passenger market. In the context of increasingly complex aircraft systems and heightened operational requirements, traditional scheduled maintenance methods can no longer deliver the safety, reliability, and cost-effectiveness needed. Predictive maintenance, which is driven by data analysis and intelligent algorithms offers a forward-looking approach to ensuring safe operation, reducing unplanned downtime, and lowering maintenance costs. This paper explores the theoretical foundations and practical applications of predictive maintenance for China's large aircraft. Through the analysis of selected case studies, we summarize the strengths and limitations of current practices and propose a feasible strategy centered on data fusion, intelligent monitoring, and collaborative decision-making. Our findings provide timely insights into further upgrading maintenance technology and strengthening overall operational assurance in the domestic aviation sector.
records.authors: Li, Xiuyi

records.title: The not-so-easy task of taking heavy-lift ML models to the edge: a performance-watt perspective
records.abstract: Edge computing is a new development paradigm that brings computational power to the network edge through novel intelligent end-user services. It allows latency-sensitive applications to be placed where the data is created, thus reducing communication overhead and improving security, mobility and power consumption. There is a plethora of applications benefiting from this type of processing. Of particular interest is emerging edge-based image classification at the microscopic level. The scale and magnitude of the objects to segment, detect and classify are very challenging, with data collected using order of magnitude in magnification. The required data processing is intense, and the wish list of end-users in this space includes tools and solutions that fit into a desk-based device. Taking heavy-lift classification models initially built in the cloud to desk-based image analysis devices is a hard job for application developers. This work looks at the performance limitations and energy consumption footprint in embedding deep learning classification models in a representative edge computing device. Particularly, the dataset and heavy-lift models explored in the case study are phytoplankton images to detect Harmful Algae Blooms (HAB) in aquaculture at early stages. The work takes a deep learning model trained for phytoplankton classification and deploys it at the edge. The embedded model, deployed in a base form alongside optimised options, is submitted to a series of system stress experiments. The performance and power consumption profiling help understand system limitations and their impact on the microscopic grade image classification task.
records.authors: Pereira, Lucas Caetano; Guterres, Bruna; Sbrissa, Kau\^{e}; Mendes, Amanda; Vermeulen, Francisca; Lain, Lisl; Smith, Mari\'{e}; Martinez, Javier; Drews, Paulo; Duarte, Nelson; Oliveira, Vinicus; Botelho, Silvia; Pias, Marcelo

records.title: The Application of Digital Twin Technology Empowered by 5G Networksand Big Data in Smart Campus
records.abstract: In the context of smart campuses, as the demand for campus services among students and faculty continues to grow, higher education institutions need to explore innovative strategies to enhance the campus living experience. Digital twin technology, by creating a virtual replica of the physical campus, enables managers to conduct simulations, analyses, and optimizations in a virtual environment, effectively guides the decision-making and operations of physical campuses, thereby providing higher education institutions with a new approach to campus management and decision support. By integrating the high-speed and low-latency characteristics of 5G networks, along with the deep analytical capabilities of big data, this paper proposes an integrated digital twin platform capable of real-time simulation of campus operations and prediction of the impact of various campus activities on resources. A study of a service application case at a certain university indicates that the combination of digital twin technology with 5G and big data significantly improves the efficiency and accuracy of campus management and enhances the quality of campus services and student experience. This study not only provides practical guidance for the implementation of digital twin technology in higher education institutions but also suggests directions for future research.
records.authors: Tong, Ming; Xiao, Peng

records.title: Research on Human-Machine Collaboration System for Intelligent Manufacturing - Based on Multi-source Data Fusion
records.abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent manufacturing, Human-Machine Collaboration Systems (HMCS) has gradually become a research hotspot as an important part of improving production efficiency and intelligence level. Based on multi-source data fusion technology, this thesis discusses the key technologies and application issues for achieving efficient human-machine collaboration in the smart manufacturing environment.The paper first introduces the basic concepts and development trends of human-machine collaborative systems, and analyses the current challenges in the field of smart manufacturing, such as data silos, delayed information transfer and insufficient collaborative efficiency. It then delves into the role of multi-source data fusion technology in these challenges, emphasising that by fusing data from different sensors, devices and systems, the decision-making capability and responsiveness of the system can be improved, thus optimising the production process.The paper further proposes a collaborative framework based on multi-source data fusion, covering key steps such as data acquisition, pre-processing, feature extraction, fusion algorithm and intelligent decision-making. On this basis, the paper experimentally verifies the application effect of the framework in the actual production environment, showing that it has significant advantages in improving production efficiency, reducing energy consumption, and improving product quality.This research not only provides a new solution for human-machine collaboration in intelligent manufacturing, but also provides a theoretical foundation and technical support for academic research and industrial practice in related fields.
records.authors: Zhao, Kun

records.title: 6G Data Analytics Platform for Applying Condition Monitoring in Smart Factory
records.abstract: 5G is the new generation of mobile communication and many scientists are doing research on it. Network Data Analytics Function (NWDAF) has been proposed to be a core function in 5G. And the intention is that NWDAF does different analysis tasks on the network data in order to improve the network functionalities and also the third-party applications. Data Science is a field of science which has gained great attention in the last years due to the rising amount of generated data and the necessity to extract information from it. Condition monitoring is an approach to maintain the machinery in industry and especially in the past years using AI/ML methods, scientists could achieve a lot in this field. In this paper we first discuss all the above mentioned topics in more detail, then we propose a data analysis platform using NWDAF in a smart factory scenario. The idea is to apply condition monitoring on the machines’ status which are connected via the 6G network.
records.authors: Arabshahi, Maryam; Schotten, Hans Dieter

records.title: System Requirements for Decentralised Collaborative Machine Learning in Industry 4.0
records.abstract: Collaborative Learning (CL) grows in relevance within Industry 4.0, as it facilitates knowledge exchange among networked participants and integrates learnings from models into local manufacturing processes. This allows organisations to efficiently harness information from distributed data, reduce costs, and accelerate innovation. Existing research focuses on conventional CL strategies, wherein model aggregation is performed on a central server. This centralised architecture, however, introduces inherent vulnerabilities, including a single point of failure and privacy risks. Recent advancements indicate a paradigm shift toward decentralised collaborative learning (DeCL) systems, yet no unified set of requirements has been proposed for supporting their development and implementation. This study addresses the aforementioned research gap by conducting a systematic literature review. Drawing on a synthesis and analysis of existing studies, this review identifies a comprehensive set of 23 system requirements, organised into six key categories, specifically focused on designing DeCL systems in manufacturing. Future research should align with Industry 5.0 principles by incorporating the human-centric design for ethical artificial intelligence and worker inclusion, as well as incorporating sustainable, resource-efficient technologies to develop environmentally responsible DeCL systems.
records.authors: Olbrych, Sylwia; Zhou, Hans Aoyang; Abdelrazeq, Anas; Schmitt, Robert H.

records.title: Digital Transformation Strategies for Power Grid Enterprises Aimed at Improving Management Efficiency
records.abstract: In promoting digital transformation in power grid enterprises, cutting-edge information technologies’ integrated applications have become crucial in supporting system performance and management efficiency. This study analyzes the comprehensive framework of digital transformation in power grid enterprises, clarifies their core driving mechanisms, and identifies key technological paths. the study establishes a data-driven power system model based on advanced approaches, including the Internet of Things, edge computing, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing. Each technology not only demonstrates its domain-specific advantages but also achieves synergistic effects through interpenetration within the system architecture, forming a multidimensional data closed-loop. After implementation, the system demonstrates remarkable performance improvements. Experimental data reveal substantial efficiency gains; management efficiency shows notable enhancement with a 65.7% reduction in response time, equipment failure rates decrease by 53.1%, and resource allocation efficiency improves by 25.5%. Regarding power supply capacity, system reliability increases by 7.5% while average downtime reduces by 68.3%. These indicator improvements collectively validate the effectiveness of technological integration. The findings further illustrate that introducing intelligent technological systems during digital transformation yields substantial benefits for power grid enterprises. This approach optimizes operation and maintenance management structures; it also provides viable paths and empirical evidence for enhancing system resilience and intelligent capabilities. The study offers both technical support and practical foundations for advancing power systems toward higher levels of automation and intelligence in future development.
records.authors: Ma, Jiaxin; Wang, Yibo; Zuo, Jing; Xu, Ruonan; Du, Wenjiao; Duan, Fang'e

records.title: Integration of Digital Twin and Federated Learning for Securing Vehicular Internet of Things
records.abstract: In the present era of advanced technology, the Internet of Things (IoT) plays a crucial role in enabling smart connected environments. This includes various domains such as smart homes, smart healthcare, smart cities, smart vehicles, and many others. The IoT facilitates the integration and interconnection of devices, enabling them to communicate, share data, and work together to create intelligent and efficient systems. With ubiquitous smart connected devices and systems, a large amount of data associated with them is at a prime risk from malicious entities (e.g., users, devices, applications) in these systems. Innovative technologies, including cloud computing, Machine Learning (ML), and data analytics, support the development of anomaly detection models for the Vehicular Internet of Things (V-IoT), which encompasses collaborative automatic driving and enhanced transportation systems. However, traditional centralized anomaly detection models fail to provide better services for connected vehicles due to issues such as high latency, privacy leakage, performance overhead, and model drift.Recently, Federated Learning (FL) has gained significant recognition for its ability to address data privacy concerns in the IoT domain. In the context of V-IoT, which involves autonomous vehicles and intelligent transportation systems with connected vehicles communicating with various sensors and devices, FL is used to develop an anomaly detection model. Current technology, the Digital Twin (DT), proves beneficial in addressing uncertain crises and data security issues by creating a virtual replica that simulates various factors, including traffic trajectories, city policies, and vehicle utilization. This enables the system to facilitate efficient and inclusive decision-making. However, the effectiveness of a V-IoT DT system heavily relies on the collection of long-term and high-quality data to make appropriate decisions. Consequently, its advantages may be limited when confronted with urgent crises like the COVID-19 pandemic.This paper introduces a Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) based anomaly detection model for V-IoT, aiming to enhance the accuracy of the model. Our proposed model integrates both DT and HFL approaches to create a comprehensive system for detecting malicious activities using an anomaly detection model. Additionally, real-world V-IoT use case scenarios are presented to demonstrate the application of the proposed model.
records.authors: Gupta, Deepti; Moni, Shafika Showkat; Tosun, Ali Saman

records.title: Quantum Computing and 6G technologies in shaping sustainable circular economy: A Preliminary study
records.abstract: Context: The quick growth of electronic devices within homes and businesses has made life better, but it has also created big problems for sustainability, like using more energy, breaking down unexpectedly, and making a lot of electronic waste. In the absence of advanced tracking and optimization methods, many products fail earlier than anticipated, undermining the operational efficiency and hindering the progress toward Circular Economy (CE) objectives. Research Problem: Key challenges lie in the limitations of conventional Internet of Things (IoT) platforms and classical computing systems, which struggles to compute vast, complex data streams generated by billions of interconnected devices. This data bottleneck impedes real-time diagnostics, predictive maintenance and effective end-of-life strategies such as reuse, repair and recycling that are essential for a functioning circular economy. Research Aim: This study explores potential of Quantum Computing (QC) and 6G-enabled ICT networks to accelerate transition to a Circular Economy (CE). We investigate their potential to enhance resource efficiency, extend product life-span and to enable advanced responsive system that support circular loop for re-use and recycling. Method: We performed a comprehensive literature review at the intersection of QC, 6G and CE, synthesizing insights to outline important pathway. Based on this review, we found thirteen important factors that explain how QC capabilities (like optimization, materials discovery, and battery innovation) work with 6G enablers (like digital twins, telemetry, and transparency). These factors are arranged into a complete framework that shows how they all affect CE drivers. Conclusion: The combined approach of QC and 6G has a lot of promise for actual-time optimization, maintenance planning, and clear lifecycle management. Using these technologies in CE practices can cut down waste, make energy usage more efficient, and promote responsible consumption, which are important factors for long-term sustainability.
records.authors: Sepehrian, Paniz; Saif, Rabia; Ghaffar, Abdullah; Akbar, Muhammad Azeem

records.title: Digital Twin and 3D Web-based Use Cases in Industry
records.abstract: Multi-physical modeling combined with data-driven decision making is giving rise to a new paradigm, the "digital twin." The digital twin is a living digital model of a system or physical asset that continuously adapts to operational changes based on real-time data. When properly designed, a digital twin can help predict the future behavior of its corresponding physical counterpart. This paper presents a series of use cases that illustrate the role of a digital twin in different stages of the industrial product lifecycle. The use cases are implemented using 3D web technology for user interfaces and web standards (X3D and glTF) for data exchange between modules. The contribution of this work consists of a set of lessons learnt and some hints on future synergies between digital twin and 3D web technologies.
records.authors: Sim\~{o}es, Bruno; Del Puy Carretero, Maria; Sanchez, Jairo; Toro, Carlos; Posada, Jorge

records.title: Insights of Oil-Gas AIoT: Core technologies and Their Significance
records.abstract: The oil and gas industry is encountering significant challenges, including inefficient data acquisition and processing within IoT frameworks, growing global energy demands, and heightened pressure to reduce environmental risks. In response, the integration of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) technologies has gained prominence across core domains such as sensing, communication, data analysis, and intelligent control. Technologies like wireless sensor networks (WSN), ZigBee, 5G, and a range of AI algorithms support end-to-end capabilities—enabling comprehensive monitoring, real-time data transmission, and automated decision-making throughout oil production operations. This integration has led to notable improvements in production efficiency and safety oversight, contributing to the broader advancement of operational intelligence within the sector.Furthermore, progress in fusion technologies is expected to accelerate the transition toward digital, intelligent, and interconnected systems, offering new momentum for sustainable development. To fully realize the potential of AIoT in the industry, targeted research and development strategies are required to address emerging technical and systemic challenges. Priorities should include reinforcing foundational research in AIoT, encouraging collaboration across sectors, and establishing unified industry standards to guide effective and secure implementation.
records.authors: Fan, Jingjing; Xing, Kaiwen; Mao, Jun; Gui, Xinyue; Li, Chengyang

records.title: Generative AI Empowered Network Digital Twins: Architecture, Technologies, and Applications
records.abstract: The rapid advancement of mobile networks highlights the limitations of traditional network planning and optimization methods, particularly in modeling, evaluation, and application. Network Digital Twins, which simulate networks in the digital domain for evaluation, offer a solution to these challenges. This concept is further enhanced by generative AI technology, which promises more efficient and accurate AI-driven data generation for network simulation and optimization. This survey provides insights into generative AI-empowered network digital twins. We begin by outlining the architecture of a network digital twin, which encompasses both digital and physical domains. This architecture involves four key steps: data processing and network monitoring, digital replication and network simulation, designing and training network optimizers, Sim2Real, and network control. Next, we systematically discuss the related studies in each step and make a detailed taxonomy of the problem studied, the methods used, and the key designs leveraged. Each step is examined with a focus on the role of generative AI, from estimating missing data and simulating network behaviors to designing control strategies and bridging the gap between digital and physical domains. Finally, we discuss the open issues and challenges of generative AI-based network digital twins.
records.authors: Li, Tong; Long, Qingyue; Chai, Haoye; Zhang, Shiyuan; Jiang, Fenyu; Liu, Haoqiang; Huang, Wenzhen; Jin, Depeng; Li, Yong

records.title: Digital Twin-based Condition Monitoring with Distributed Data Mapping of OPC UA and ISO 10303 STEP Standard
records.abstract: A digital twin (DT), the digital counterpart of a physical entity, process, or system, is a pivotal innovation driving the manufacturing industry’s digital transformation. DT plays a significant role in product lifecycle management (PLM) and product condition monitoring. However, the diversity of systems and processes involved poses challenges in DT and data management within PLM, particularly regarding efficiency, standardized data mapping, and latency. The paper presents a solution architecture to address these challenges and contribute towards an efficient and cost-effective product lifecycle management system. The architecture focuses on DT’s data management and communication aspects, utilizing the edge-based, decentralized Eclipse Arrowhead Framework and EDMtruePLM (Enterprise Data Management True Product Lifecycle Management) for standardized data management and condition monitoring of products. Integrating the ISO 10303 STEP standard for data modeling and the Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) standard for communication is emphasized, improving the contextual significance of the data and the system’s interoperability. A use case implementation is presented, where a fischertechnik assembly line is monitored, capturing sensor data through the PLC’s OPC UA server. The sensor data is then aligned with the STEP standard and stored in the EDMTruePLM database for monitoring.
records.authors: Tripathy, Aparajita; Chevuri, Rishyank; Tran, Tuan; Acharya, Sarthak; Deventer, Jan van; Paniagua, Cristina; Delsing, Jerker

records.title: Service Computing for Industry 4.0: State of the Art, Challenges, and Research Opportunities
records.abstract: Recent advances in the large-scale adoption of information and communication technologies in manufacturing processes, known as Industry 4.0 or Smart Manufacturing, provide us a window into how the manufacturing sector will evolve in the coming decades. As a result of these initiatives, manufacturing firms have started to integrate a series of emerging technologies into their processes that will change the way products are designed, manufactured, and consumed. This article provides a comprehensive review of how service-oriented computing is being employed to develop the required software infrastructure for Industry 4.0 and identifies the major challenges and research opportunities that ensue. Particular attention is paid to the microservices architecture, which is increasingly recognized as offering a promising approach for developing innovative industrial applications. This literature review is based on the current state of the art on service computing for Industry 4.0 as described in a large corpus of recently published research papers, which helped us to identify and explore a series of challenges and opportunities for the development of this emerging technology frontier, with the goal of facilitating its widespread adoption.
records.authors: Siqueira, Frank; Davis, Joseph G.

records.title: AI-Based intelligent edge autonomous control technology for energy conservation and carbon reduction in smart public buildings
records.abstract: Under the “Dual Carbon” goals, public buildings represent a major sector for energy consumption and carbon emissions in the construction industry, making energy-efficient and low-carbon development of public buildings a critical priority for China's low-carbon urban development objectives. To address challenges such as the lack of real-time user behavior interaction, prolonged operation of HVAC and lighting systems in unoccupied spaces, and inappropriate temperature settings in public buildings. This study proposes an AI-based intelligent edge autonomous control system for smart public buildings. This system, designed around user behavior, integrates artificial intelligence, machine learning, the Internet of Things (IoT), big data, cloud computing, and digital twin technologies to establish a real-time, self-updating building model with automated control. It could ensure compatibility between public building environments and user scenarios while delivering an effective solution for energy conservation and carbon reduction. The system employs millimeter-wave radar sensors to  autonomously  detect and assess  occupancy, temperature, humidity, illuminance, and air quality within public building spaces. Additionally, it utilizes AI-powered edge computing to perform 24/7 automated decision-making for offices, meeting rooms, and open areas based on zonal management objectives and user behavior patterns, issuing real-time control commands to terminal devices to achieve energy and emission reductions. A pilot implementation in an office building validated the system's feasibility, with energy performance data demonstrating that the intelligent edge autonomous control system enables zonal management, effectively resolving delays in environmental energy management and minimizing energy waste. The system reduces operational energy consumption and carbon emissions by over 25%, confirming its significant impact on public building sustainability.
records.authors: Ruan, Ruolin

records.title: The Mechanism of Mobile Communication Technology Prompting Digital Transformation of Manufacturing Industry: From the Perspective of Data Factor Empowerment
records.abstract: Abstract: The digital transformation of manufacturing industry is a crucial measure for achieving high-quality development, and mobile communication technology plays a significant role in this process. This paper focuses on exploring the internal mechanism of mobile communication technology promoting the digital transformation of manufacturing industry, with a particular emphasis on three major technologies: 5G, 5G-A, and 6G. Firstly, the paper summarizes the latest progress of mobile communication technology in the field of manufacturing digital transformation. Secondly, it outlines the characteristics of technological evolution from 5G to 6G. Thirdly, based on the technological evolution process, it presents the three major capabilities of 6G, namely transmission, integrated sensing and communication, and intelligent computing. It further elaborates on how mobile communication technology gives rise to data facotor and clarifies the internal mechanism of mobile communication technology enabling data factor to empower the digital transformation of manufacturing industry. Finally, it looks forward to the typical development trends of 6G in the field of manufacturing digital transformation.
records.authors: Li, Ran; Wei, Muhua; Liu, Huili; Qi, Jiayin; Liu, Lina

records.title: Model Driven Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, and DevOps for Software and Systems Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study of Synergies and Challenges
records.abstract: This paper presents a systematic mapping study classifying existing scientific contributions on synergies of Model Driven Engineering (MDE), Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML), and DevOps, with the overall objective of supporting the continuous development of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs). We collected papers from bibliographic sources and selected primary studies to analyse. Then, we characterised and classified the current state of the art, focusing on 1) main aspects already tackled at the intersection of at least two of the three studied areas, and 2) findings emerging from the analysis as a framework for potential future research, notably regarding the integration of the three studied areas. The results reveal that few approaches combine MDE, AI/ML, and DevOps for software and systems engineering. In contrast, several approaches have combined two of them, specifically MDE and DevOps. Approaches combining AI/ML with MDE or DevOps are also becoming more frequent and will most likely continue to progress in the future. These synergies cover a range of engineering activities, from requirements and design to monitoring, maintenance, and evolution. Open research challenges include advancing AI/ML, MDE, and DevOps integration, supporting scalable, data-oriented solutions, proposing new continuous engineering methods, and adapting DevOps practices to diverse systems.
records.authors: Berardinelli, Luca; Muttillo, Vittoriano; Eramo, Romina; Bruneliere, Hugo; Rahimi, Abbas; Cicchetti, Antonio; Giner-Miguelez, Joan; G\'{o}mez, Abel; Potena, Pasqualina; Saadatmand, Mehrdad

records.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Deep Learning-based Predictive Maintenance
records.abstract: With the advent of Industrial 4.0 and the push toward Industry 5.0, the data generated by the industries have become surprisingly large. This abundance of data significantly boosts machine and deep learning models for Predictive Maintenance (PdM). The PdM plays a vital role in extending the lifespan of industrial equipment and machines while also helping to reduce the risk of unscheduled downtime. Given its multidisciplinary nature, the field of PdM has been approached from many different angles: this comprehensive survey aims at providing an up-to-date overview focused on all the learning-based industrial PdM strategies, discussing weaknesses and strengths. The survey is based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodological flow, allowing a systematic and complete review of the literature. In particular, firstly, we explore the main learning models used for PdM, mainly Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets), Autoencoders (AEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and Transformers, also giving an overview of the newest models such as diffusion models and foundation models. Then, we discuss the main learning paradigms applied to PdM, i.e., supervised, unsupervised, ensemble, transfer, federated, and reinforcement learning. Furthermore, this work discusses the pipeline of the data-driven PdM and its benefits, practical applications, datasets, and benchmarks. In addition, the evaluation metrics for each PdM stage and the state-of-the-art hardware devices used are discussed. Finally, the challenges and future work are presented.
records.authors: Khan, Uzair; Cheng, Dong Seon; Setti, Francesco; Fummi, Franco; Cristani, Marco; Capogrosso, Luigi

records.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on IoT Application Technology Talent Demand
records.abstract: AI's deployment across IoT has transformed several industries and introduced complexities requiring a drastic shift in the skill set expected from IoT application technology talent. Within this context, this paper, contributing to the literature by providing a comprehensive review on the impact of AI on IoT talent demand, covering the evolving skills requirements, industry trends and educational implications. By synthesizing the output of existing literature, industry reports, and case studies, we highlight the essential skills sought after and some hurdles to the industry adapting to this change. We also provide actionable steps to bridge the skill gap and outline the future directions for research and practice in this space. Key Features of AI: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Image Processing. AI technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and more have made it possible to create advanced IoT applications. From predictive maintenance and autonomous decision-making to real-time data analytics, these applications have disrupted traditional industries and spawned new business models. AI in Manufacturing. For example, in manufacturing, AI is being used for predictive maintenance and quality control, which minimizes equipment downtime and improvements in product quality. In the medical field, AI-empowered IoT devices provide remote patient monitoring and predictive analysis, enhancing patient care and enhancing medical outcomes. In retail, IoT devices that use AI offer personalized recommendations and intelligent inventory management, improving customer experiences while making stores more efficient. While AI and the Internet of Things (IoT) present powerful opportunities in terms of their applications, the industry also has its challenges, especially in terms of talent demand. There is a rising demand for AI and IoT professionals in the integration of IoT systems with AI. There is, however, a significant skills gap, as many organizations face difficulties in finding candidates with the necessary interdisciplinary expertise. This skills gap mean therefore lead to project implementation time delays and added costs, preventing the realization of the full potential of AI that powers IoT applications. The findings of this study not only highlight the key trends of AI influence on IoT but also assist major stakeholders including educators, practitioners and students to develop matching strategies to adapt to the transformations brought by the AI technologies in the specific context of the IoT. As AI and IoT continue to evolve and converge, their potential for creating impactful and transformative solutions will only grow.
records.authors: Su, Zijie

records.title: Analysis the Research Hotspots and Key Technical of Intelligent Manufacturing
records.abstract: Intelligent manufacturing is one of the keys to open up the future of life, and multidisciplinary interactions have shown its strong vitality. This study conducts a scientometric review of the global research published since 1987 on intelligent manufacturing, through citation, keyword, clustering and keywords burst analysis. A total of 3994 research documents are taken as data sources, which are retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database from 1987 to 2021. Using the CiteSpace analysis tool, this paper discussed the development process of the relevant years of intelligent manufacturing, analyzed the research hotspots and their technology, presented the emerging models and techniques, and identified the latest research evolution and trends. The results will provide reference for scientific scholars in future research in the field of intelligent manufacturing.
records.authors: Cai, Yu; Wu, Jiahao; Zaheer, Muhammad

records.title: Physio-Digital Twin for Human-Centered IoT Mobility: A Proof-of-Concept Implementation on the E-Bike Platform
records.abstract: Human-centered Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are becoming increasingly critical for sustainable mobility and health monitoring. This paper presents the design and proof of concept of a Physio-Digital Twin (PDT) integrated into the E-Bike platform, combining physiological sensing (heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV)), embedded artificial intelligence, and adaptive mobility control. The PDT models a rider’s physiological and behavioral state in real time to dynamically adjust electric-assist torque and lighting conditions. Building upon recent advancements in Human Digital Twins (HDTs) for rehabilitation and generative-AI-enabled IoT-healthcare frameworks, this study demonstrates how physiological feedback can enhance both user well-being and system sustainability. A single-participant proof of concept demonstrates the feasibility of the approach; preliminary trends suggest lower HRV-derived stress and higher perceived comfort under adaptive operation. These qualitative findings highlight the potential of embedding human physiological intelligence directly into IoT-based mobility systems and motivate broader, multi-participant validation.
records.authors: Shah, Syed Tahir Ali; Santos, Jos\'{e} Paulo Oliveira; Constantinescu, Gabriel; Fernandes, Jos\'{e} Maria Amaral; Pereira, Antonio Manuel de Bastos

records.title: Context-driven Edge-based Data Sharing for Industrial IoT Data Spaces
records.abstract: The increasing reliance on IoT ecosystems demands robust, secure, and context-aware data-sharing mechanisms that operate closer to data sources. Data spaces must leverage trusted edge-based system architectures for near real-time data processing, transformation, and enrichment while ensuring data privacy and security. However, the current International Data Spaces (IDS) Model lacks comprehensive support for Edge-based architectures and flexible, context-driven access control models essential for managing diverse applications within data space ecosystems.To address these gaps, we propose IDS4Edge, an IDS-compliant approach that enables dynamic, context-driven, Edge-based IoT data sharing as a service. IDS4Edge integrates flexible access control policies on top of IDS connectors, tailored to specific IoT application contexts. These policies dynamically adapt in real-time to changes in IoT contexts and contractual agreements, ensuring secure and efficient data sharing at the Edge.We validate our solution through a proof-of-concept implementation, demonstrating how IDS4Edge facilitates trusted, scalable, and real-time data sharing while maintaining compliance with IDS principles. This approach paves the way for enhanced (industrial) IoT applications and advanced data-sharing paradigms, such as Manufacturing-as-a-Service (MaaS).
records.authors: Lam, An Ngoc; Nguyen, Phu H.; Ma, Xiang

records.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Interoperability for IIoT: Taxonomy, Standards, and Future Directions
records.abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, the Internet-of-Things (IoT) performs the driving position analogous to the initial industrial metamorphosis. IoT affords the potential to couple machine-to-machine intercommunication and real-time information-gathering within the industry domain. Hence, the enactment of IoT in the industry magnifies effective optimization, authority, and data-driven judgment. However, this field undergoes several interoperable issues, including large numbers of heterogeneous IoT gadgets, tools, software, sensing, and processing components, joining through the Internet, despite the deficiency of communication protocols and standards. Recently, various interoperable protocols, platforms, standards, and technologies are enhanced and altered according to the specifications of the applicability in industrial applications. However, there are no recent survey papers that primarily examine various interoperability issues that Industrial IoT (IIoT) faces. In this review, we investigate the conventional and recent developments of relevant state-of-the-art IIoT technologies, frameworks, and solutions for facilitating interoperability between different IIoT components. We also discuss several interoperable IIoT standards, protocols, and models for digitizing the industrial revolution. Finally, we conclude this survey with an inherent discussion of open challenges and directions for future research.
records.authors: Hazra, Abhishek; Adhikari, Mainak; Amgoth, Tarachand; Srirama, Satish Narayana

records.title: Research on Enhancing Enterprise Resource Management Efficiency Using Digital Twin Technology
records.abstract: As power enterprises undergo rapid digital transformation, traditional resource management methods increasingly fail to meet the demands of real-time and intelligent system operations. Digital twin technology, which creates virtual replicas of physical assets, offers an opportunity to improve efficiency. This paper proposes a digital twin–based framework tailored to power enterprises, integrating lifecycle modeling, real-time data synchronization, and intelligent dispatch algorithms for precise coordination of personnel, materials, and equipment. A deployment at a regional power grid company showed a 23% improvement in work order processing, an 18% increase in fault prediction accuracy, and a 26% reduction in resource allocation response time. These findings highlight the potential of this framework to advance intelligent resource management in the power sector and provide valuable insights for broader adoption of digital twin technology.
records.authors: Jiang, Jiang

records.title: Using simulation and digital twins to innovate: are we getting smarter?
records.abstract: Digital Twins have recently emerged as a major new area of innovation. Digital Twins are often found at the core of "smart" solutions that have also emerged as major areas of innovation. Modeling and Simulation (M&S) approaches create a model of a real-world system that is linked to data sources and is used to simulate and predict the behavior of its real-world counterpart. On the face of it Digital Twins and M&S appear to be similar, if not the same. Is this actually the case? Are the two fields really separate or is Digital Twin research re-inventing the "M&S wheel"? To investigate these relationships, in this panel we will explore some contemporary innovations with Digital Twins and discuss whether or not Digital Twins is a contemporary "refresh" or "rebranding" of M&S or if there are exciting new synergies.
records.authors: Taylor, Simon J E; Johansson, Bjorn; Jeon, Sumin; Lee, Loo Hay; Lendermann, Peter; Shao, Guodong

records.title: Industrial Internet of Things Ecosystems Security and Digital Forensics: Achievements, Open Challenges, and Future Directions
records.abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has been positioned as a key pillar of the Industry 4.0 revolution, which is projected to continue accelerating and realizing digital transformations. The IIoT is becoming indispensable, providing the means through which modern communication is conducted across industries and offering improved efficiency, scalability, and robustness. However, the structural and dynamic complexity introduced by the continuous integration of the IIoT has widened the scope for cyber-threats, as the processes and data generated by this integration are susceptible and vulnerable to attacks. This article presents an in-depth analysis of the state-of-the-art in the IIoT ecosystem from security and digital forensics perspectives. The dimensions of this study are twofold: first, we present an overview of the cutting-edge security of IIoT ecosystems, and second, we survey the literature on digital forensics. The key achievements, open challenges, and future directions are identified in each case. The challenges and directions for future studies that we identify will provide important guidance for cybersecurity researchers and practitioners.
records.authors: Kebande, Victor R.; Awad, Ali Ismail

records.title: The Architecture of AI and Communication Integration towards 6G: An O-RAN Evolution
records.abstract: The evolution of communication architecture shifts towards virtualization and cloud-native network functions, setting the stage for the flexibility and integration of emerging technologies. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) as intrinsic elements in network design are some of the crucial visions and requirements for 6G. This paper, from the perspective of O-RAN, explores how current network architectures should evolve towards the integration of communication and intelligence in 6G. It begins with a comprehensive analysis and comparison of the AI-related work conducted by various standard organizations. Building on this, an end-to-end AI integration framework is proposed, which leverages AI technologies, data services, and digital twin (DT) technologies to achieve an integrated intelligent 6G communication system. After that, the key enabling technologies for cross-domain AI, service-based RAN, programmable RAN and digital twins are discussed. At last, the paper analyzes the challenges and opportunities for O-RAN evolution.
records.authors: Li, Zexu; Wang, Qingtian; Wang, Yue; Chen, Tao

records.title: Research on the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Mechanical Engineering Design Optimization
records.abstract: AI has demonstrated unprecedented potential for advancement in mechanical engineering design optimization, particularly in key areas such as generative design, additive manufacturing, simulation acceleration, digital twins, and automated design. Algorithms automatically generate and optimize diverse design patterns, transcending the limitations of traditional topology optimization. Structural design has achieved a leap beyond human intuition. For additive manufacturing, AI leverages real-time data to intelligently optimize process parameters and defect detection, significantly enhancing production efficiency and quality. Digital twins facilitate instant communication between virtual models and actual systems, facilitating the implementation of intelligent manufacturing and predictive maintenance. While AI technology holds great potential, practical applications still face challenges such as insufficient data, model interpretability, high computational costs, a shortage of interdisciplinary talent, and ethical considerations. This article explores these challenges and proposes strategies such as data sharing, explainable AI, human-machine integration, green AI, educational reform, and ethical management. With the advancement of AI technology, mechanical design will gradually transition to a data- and model-driven phase, facilitating the growth of intelligent, flexible, and sustainable manufacturing systems and injecting new impetus into the industrial revolution.
records.authors: Ru, Yiwen

records.title: Research on the Construction of Industrial Robot Digital Twin Course Driven by “Dual-Subject & Six-Cooperation” Mechanism
records.abstract: Accelerated upgrading of the intelligent manufacturing industry intensifies demand for talents proficient in industrial robot digital twin technology, yet traditional courses face core challenges: superficial school-enterprise collaboration, disconnected training-production, and static evaluation systems. Guided by the dual-system theory of vocational education, virtual-physical integration teaching theory, and digital twin principles, this study proposes the “Dual-Subject & Six-Cooperation” mechanism (led by vocational colleges and enterprises, encompassing joint research on curriculum standards, co-construction of teaching resources, co-training of faculty teams, shared responsibility for practical tasks, joint discussion on evaluation systems, and two-way sharing of achievements). It employs a four-dimensional digital twin system (physical entity, virtual model, data link, training module) as the technical carrier, integrating key computer technologies including 3D modeling, EKF filtering, and OPC UA real-time interaction. The study further constructs a five-in-one curriculum system (“Mechanism-Technology-Curriculum-Teaching-Evaluation”), covering post competency mapping, a four-layer technical architecture, three-level curriculum modules, a four-stage teaching process, and LSTM-driven tripartite dynamic evaluation. This work aims to address traditional teaching pain points, achieve in-depth coupling of industrial demands with educational supply, and provide a unique technical paradigm and theoretical support for integrating the proposed “Dual-Subject & Six-Cooperation” mechanism with computer technologies in industrial robot vocational curriculum reform.
records.authors: Lu, Yanru

records.title: Research on Transparency Mechanism of Manufacturing Supply Chain Finance Based on Digital Twin and Blockchain
records.abstract: Manufacturing supply chain finance has long faced core problems such as information asymmetry, difficult credit evaluation, and insufficient transparency, which seriously restrict the financing efficiency and cost control of small and medium-sized enterprises. This study proposes a transparency mechanism for manufacturing supply chain finance that integrates digital twin and blockchain technologies. Through digital twin technology, real-time mapping between supply chain physical entities and digital space is achieved, combined with the decentralized characteristics of blockchain to build a trusted data storage and smart contract execution environment. The research establishes a three-layer system architecture, designs a supply chain health evaluation model based on weighted comprehensive evaluation and a dynamic credit scoring system, and verifies the effectiveness of the mechanism through simulation experiments. Experimental results show that compared with traditional modes, this mechanism reduces financing approval time by 96.808%, reduces annualized financing interest rates by 3.270 percentage points, controls bad debt rates within 0.847%, and improves supply chain transparency index to 0.912.
